---
engine: markdown
title: Your First Model
description: Predict whether a payment will be disputed, from its amount and merchant.
---

Start with one payment and one outcome: will this payment receive a dispute
within the next 30 days?
A risk team needs this estimate while the payment is still being processed,
so it can decide which payments deserve review. Historical outcomes teach the
model; new payments supply only the evidence available at that decision.

Begin with the relationship between amount, merchant, and the later outcome
across past payments. This first model has no account history. The next
tutorial puts this payment and its predecessors in one transaction branch,
with a dispute target on every item.

You need Python 3.12 or newer. Install relflow in your project:

```bash
uv add relflow
```

## Describe One Payment

Each training record contains the information available at payment time and
the outcome observed later:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
disputed: false
```

## Define The Fields

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

`Number` represents the amount, `Category` represents the merchant, and
`Boolean` represents the yes-or-no outcome. `mask=True` marks `disputed` as
a prediction target: the model learns from its value without seeing it as
an input. `Model.xs` supplies a small model configuration.

```{typst}
//| label: fig-first-payment
//| fig-alt: "A payment has amount and merchant input fields, and a disputed Boolean prediction target."
//| fig-cap: "Two input fields support one prediction."
#tree(node("payment", kind: "root", children: (
  node("amount", type: "Number"),
  node("merchant", type: "Category"),
  node("disputed", kind: "target", type: "Boolean"),
)))
```

## Train The Model

Use your application's Parquet files, with one payment per row and the three
columns above. Train on earlier payments and validate on a later period;
both splits include the observed `disputed` labels.

```python
data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=model,
    train="payments/train.parquet",
    validate="payments/validation.parquet",
)
model.fit(data, batch_size=128, max_epochs=20)
```

`batch_size=128` sets the number of payments per training batch on each device.
relflow configures the training loop, stops early when validation loss stops
improving, and restores the best validation checkpoint.

## Predict New Payments

The request file contains `amount` and `merchant`. It omits `disputed`,
because that is the outcome you want to predict.

```python
requests = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=model,
    predict="payments/requests.parquet",
)
predictions = model.predict(datamodule=requests, batch_size=256, devices=1)
```

`devices=1` collects the predictions on one device. `predictions` is an Arrow
table. Read the target under `predictions.disputed`.
[Prediction Output](guides/prediction-output.qmd) explains its probability and
the difference from earlier address-keyed output.

Next, [add transaction history](tutorials/transaction-history.qmd) to move the
payment fields into `trxns` and score each transaction using the shared
account context. For training options and saving your model, see
[Training And Checkpoints](guides/lightning.qmd).
